---

I made the change. The `GET /parcels` default page size is now 100.

**What changed**
- `api/pagination.py:8` changed `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` from 50 to 100.
- `tests/test_pagination.py` now asserts 100 in `test_default_page_size`.

I ran the full test suite, not only the pagination test. The pass/fail output is above, as it came out. I also searched the docs and API spec files for any text that still says the default is 50. Those results are above as well.

**Why the risk is low**
- No other code reads `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`, so the change cannot spread into other modules.
- 100 is still well under `MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 500`, so no limit check is affected.
- It is a one-line revert if you need to roll back.

**What your manager may want to watch after deploy**
- Clients that do not send a page size will now get twice as many parcels per response. Responses will be larger and may be a little slower.
- A client that counted on exactly 50 items per page could act differently. One example is a client that stops paging when it gets fewer than 50 items. That is the main behavior change. The code itself is low risk.

One more note: this directory is not a git repository, so there is no commit to point to for review or rollback. Do you want me to `git init` and commit this change so it has a clean record?

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Changing a default is a behavior change for clients, even when the diff is one line. Only clients that leave the parameter out see the new value. That makes them easy to miss in testing.
- Keeping `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` and `MAX_PAGE_SIZE` side by side in one module helps here. You can confirm that the new default still fits under the cap in one glance.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
